content.value_statement: TypeScript changes can lose safety when teams use broad types, casts, or unclear models. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward Metabase-specific typing patterns and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Applies a strict no-any rule for new TypeScript and JavaScript changes.
Guides type tightening with generics, utility types, and boundary typing.
Encourages reuse of Metabase domain types and generated API types.
Models async, null, optional, and variant states with explicit TypeScript types.
Promotes small functions, reusable helpers, and clear component extraction.
Requires TypeScript language server inspection and project type-checking after edits.
limitations: It provides coding guidance and does not run tools by itself.
It depends on shared Metabase workflow files for command details.
It is tailored to Metabase conventions and may not fit other repositories.
It does not replace human review for product behavior or API contract decisions.

use_cases.title: Refactor weak TypeScript safely
use_cases.description: Replace casts, any types, and broad records with narrower signatures and reusable domain types.

use_cases.title: Model UI state precisely
use_cases.description: Represent loading, error, empty, and success states with discriminated unions and exhaustive checks.

use_cases.title: Review JavaScript migration scope
use_cases.description: Identify when touched JavaScript should become TypeScript before feature work continues.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a simple function
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for safer typing in one function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to improve this function without introducing any. Keep the signature narrow and explain the type changes briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor component props
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for React component cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to refactor these React props. Prefer existing Metabase types, avoid casts, and keep optional values precise.

prompt_templates.title: Model async state
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for UI state modeling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to model this async UI state with a discriminated union. Include exhaustive handling and avoid broad string states.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a JavaScript migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before changing an existing JavaScript file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to assess this JavaScript file. Propose a separate TypeScript conversion plan before implementing the feature change.

output_examples.input: A component receives a broad object but only reads an id and name.
output_examples.output: The response narrows the prop shape to the required fields, reuses domain id types, and removes unnecessary casts.

output_examples.input: A feature uses separate booleans for loading, error, and data states.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a discriminated union with exhaustive rendering paths for loading, error, success, and empty states.

output_examples.input: A JavaScript file needs a feature change.
output_examples.output: The response recommends converting the file to TypeScript in a separate change before adding the feature.

best_practices: Start by finding existing Metabase types before defining new shapes.
Use unknown at system boundaries and narrow it immediately with typed guards.
Run the TypeScript language server checks and project type-check before finishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use any, double casts, or broad records to silence compiler errors.
Do not duplicate generated API types or redefine shared type guards locally.
Do not thread undefined through many layers when it can be narrowed at the source.

faq.question: Does this skill write TypeScript code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides an AI coding agent while it writes or refactors TypeScript and JavaScript. The agent still performs the edits.

faq.question: Is any ever allowed?
faq.answer: The skill treats any as forbidden for new code. Boundary values should use declared types, unknown, guards, or typed wrappers.

faq.question: Can this skill be used outside Metabase?
faq.answer: Some TypeScript advice is general, but many rules reference Metabase types, folders, and workflow expectations.

faq.question: What verification does it require?
faq.answer: It asks the agent to inspect changed symbols with the TypeScript Language Server and run the project type-check.

faq.question: How does it handle existing JavaScript files?
faq.answer: It recommends proposing a separate TypeScript conversion before making feature changes in existing JavaScript files.

faq.question: Does it include security-sensitive behavior?
faq.answer: No evidence was found for command execution, network access, or prompt injection. The content is coding guidance in Markdown.
